reviews.comment: 318 was the worst structured college class I have ever been in. The only grades are Exams. Professor does not give any study guides, guidance for what is on the tests, and she made it clear no extra credit will be given out. Attendance is mandatory, and exams are VERY difficult. A good chunk of students dropped after the 2nd exam. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ureta has been one of my favorite professors at TAMU. She is incredibly well versed and passionate about what she teaches. Grades were composed of four exams. Attend lectures (they are very interesting!) and definitely read the readings she assigns, they are heavily tested. If you go to class and put in effort you can get a good grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gives good lectures, not just reading off slides provided by a text book company, so showing up and listening is a must if you want an A. Exams are easy as long as you pay attention in class and can solve algebra equations. Applies content to real world policies, making the class more practical.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ureta's class is only bad if you're looking for a blow-off class. She's here to teach, and she does it well. The class is just based on test grades, so study up and pay close attention to the problem sets she gives. For theory questions, she usually just took graphs from the textbook.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She expects you to read the textbook a lot and to understand every tangent that she goes on and tests you on it. She grades hard as well and doesn't really give you any points for trying. The tests are a lot harder than they need to be. I would not like to take this professor again.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Ureta super sweet and cares a lot about students. I never read the textbook just attend lectures AND READ THE ARTICLES SHE ASSIGNS! The articles are like 50% of the exam questions. This was one of the easiest econ electives I've ever taken. I highly recommend this course as an econ elective. If you're not an econ major don't take it.

Hypocritical expectations for students. Severely rebukes if you forget a date but she often makes the exact same mistake herself. Also does not foster an environment that is conducive for learning. Discourages students by readily ridiculing them when they engage.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this professor. I am now a senior ECON student and this would have been my only C I have ever recieved. Thank God for pass/fail the Spring 2020 semester. Her test questions she will never actually cover in class. Teach everything yourself. Read the textbook thoroughly, as she will pull the most random things from it on test. AVOID PROF.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dreaded going to this class. She's condescending and a hard grader- expect rude comments on your papers. Tests are over small details in the papers or lectures so it was hard to prepare for exams. 6 exams total & 2 papers. Do NOT take this class unless you absolutely must and can't take anything else. She rambles a lot but concepts aren't hard.
Dr. Ureta is a great professor. Disregard negative comments about her. She is very straight forward with what sh expects from you from class, only grades are exams and she drops the lowest grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Having just completed 114 hours and as economics major, this is my second C ever. Attendance is not mandatory so people quit going to class and she may change that but her lectures are EXTREMELY boring. She has a super soft voice, hates when students ask questions and is very political. I would suggest not taking this class unless it it mandatory.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't bother going to lectures, all she does is ramble up until time's up. All her grades are cumulative of 4 tests. I recommend just reading the textbook because the practice problem she gives will most likely not appear on the test.

I took her for Gender and Race. She have a quiz every week and those were our only grades and she dropped the lowest two. Attendance wasn't mandatory but she gave extra credit if you didn't miss more than 2 classes. I enjoyed her class and the quizzes weren't too bad. You HAVE to read the articles to pass though. I recommend!

Do NOT take ECON/WGST318 if you are NOT strong in Econ. I took her class as an elective and found that you need a strong background in econ, stats and cal.  I had to drop it because I was putting so much effort into her class that my other classes were suffering. She is NOT sympathetic OR understanding. NO EXCUSES. But, she is reasonable.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Ureta is very smart and a very good lecturer. However, do not ask questions in her class. She doesn't like to answer questions and will act like your question is stupid. Read the textbook, and do practice problems or you will not do well in this class. Go to class everyday. Attendance optional but she records it. You will have to work for an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gender and Race, explains everything so you can understand it. She is not forgiving. My writing is not the greatest though. When I really tried at my absolute hardest, I got accused of cheating and was told to re-write it. TIPS: go to class, take notes, and do not use ANY electronics or she will shun you for the rest of the semester.

Prof.Ureta is extremely fair.  You always know where you stand in here class because her 3 exams are curved to average 75 and you are expected to improve your grade with homework scores. No final curve.  If you miss 3 or less classes you get 2 points added to your final grade.  She knows her stuff and uses alot of current examples in her class.

Ureta - is a good teacher. However, she can tends to move rather quickly. She doesn't seem very approachable, and when you ask questions, she still fails to clarify the answer.  I would take her for undergraduate econometrics, but not graduate.
